title: GOD MAKES ROOM FOR THE POOR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If anyone making the vow is too poor to pay the specified amount, they
are to present the person to the priest, who will set the value for them
according to what the one making the vow can afford'" - Lev 27:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a moment of great tenderness in the middle of a list of prices.
What about the person who wanted to make a vow to God but simply could
not afford the set amount? God did not shut them out. The priest would
adjust the value according to what they could afford.

Think about what this reveals. God never intended devotion to be a
privilege only the wealthy could afford. The poor worshipper's vow was
just as welcome as the rich one's. The amount was scaled to the person's
means, so no one was excluded by poverty.

Dear friend, this same heart runs all through Scripture. When Mary and
Joseph brought Jesus to the temple, they offered two doves — the
provision God had made specifically for those too poor to afford a lamb
(Luke 2:24; Lev 12:8). The Saviour of the world was born into a family
that qualified for the poor person's offering.

Jesus watched a widow drop two tiny coins into the treasury and declared
she had given more than all the wealthy (Mark 12:43-44). God measures
giving by the heart, not the amount.

If you have ever felt you have too little to offer God — too little
money, too little talent, too little strength — this verse is for you.
Bring what you can. God receives the honest gift of the poor with as much
delight as the great gift of the rich.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I felt I have too little to offer God?
2. Do I measure giving by amount rather than by heart?
3. How can my church make sure no one is excluded by poverty?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You receive the gift of the poor as gladly as the
gift of the rich. I bring You what I can, trusting that You measure the
heart. Amen.
